'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2024 Kharkiv offensive]]
***Seven people are killed and at least 28 others are injured in [[Russia]]n [[missile]] strikes in [[Liubotyn]] and [[Kharkiv]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-attack-ukraines-kharkiv-kills-two-injures-least-seven-governor-says-2024-05-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***At least two people are killed in a [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] missile strike on [[Alushta]], [[Crimea]]. Explosions are reported across the peninsula and Ukrainian media reports that multiple targets were hit. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/two-dead-ukrainian-missile-attack-head-russia-annexed-crimea-says-2024-05-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[Eastern Ukraine campaign]]
***Russian forces captures the village of [[Andriivka, Bakhmut Raion, Donetsk Oblast|Andriivka]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/05/23/russia-ukraine-latest-blinken-missiles/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***At least 60 [[Palestinians]] are killed in [[Israel]]i attacks in [[Rafah]], [[Deir al-Balah]], and [[Gaza City]], [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://aje.io/hg54p3 (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Pope Francis]] and the [[Dicastery for the Causes of Saints]] approves the [[canonization]] of [[Carlo Acutis]], who will become the first [[millennial]] saint. [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2024/05/23/240523b.html (Holy See)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd11kyy58dgo (BBC News)]
*Romanian author [[Mircea Cărtărescu]] wins the [[International Dublin Literary Award]] for his novel ''[[Solenoid (novel)|Solenoid]]'', translated by Sean Cotter. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/article/2024/may/24/100000-dublin-literary-award-won-by-romanian-author-mircea-cartarescu (''The Guardian'')] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Thane explosion]]
**Ten people are killed and 64 others are injured after an explosion of four boilers at a chemical factory in [[Dombivili]], [[India]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/video/massive-explosion-fire-at-factory-in-thane-at-least-20-evacuated-787309 (NDTV)]
*Eleven people are killed and two others are injured in an explosion at a [[sugar]] [[factory]] in [[Morogoro]], [[Tanzania]]. [https://apnews.com/article/tanzania-sugar-factory-blast-mtibwa-317295def5aa83ef4069c33467bdef8e (AP)]
*Four people are killed and 16 others are injured when the second floor of a restaurant collapses in [[Palma de Mallorca]], [[Spain]]. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-mallorca-building-collapse-deaths-tourists-3acf4103d7e00ed569c56a7fe8e02665 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[China]]'s [[People's Liberation Army]] begins two days of [[military exercise|military drills]] around [[Taiwan]]. In response, Taiwan mobilizes [[Republic of China Armed Forces|its military]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqvv29gpqn1o (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/china-starts-military-drills-around-taiwan-days-after-new-president-takes-office-2024-05-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[List of diplomatic missions to Palestine|Diplomatic missions to Palestine]]
**[[President of Colombia|Colombian President]] [[Gustavo Petro]] orders the opening of an [[embassy]] in [[Ramallah]] in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/23/colombias-petro-orders-embassy-to-open-in-west-banks-ramallah (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kenya–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces during a state visit by [[President of Kenya|Kenyan President]] [[William Ruto]] that he will designate [[Kenya]] a [[major non-NATO ally]] as it is expected to lead the [[Multinational Security Support Mission in Haiti|international intervention in Haiti]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-expected-designate-kenya-major-non-nato-ally-source-says-2024-05-22/ (Reuters)] [https://www.npr.org/biden-kenya-state-visit (NPR)]
*Russia removes the border markers signaling the border with [[Estonia]] on the [[Narva River]], prompting a protest by the EU. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c899844ypj2o (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*''[[United States v. Live Nation Entertainment]]''
**The [[United States Department of Justice]] sues [[Ticketmaster]] and its parent company [[Live Nation (events promoter)|Live Nation]], seeking the breakup of the company and accusing the company of creating a [[monopoly]] by eliminating competition and increasing prices. [https://apnews.com/article/justice-department-live-nation-ticketmaster-antitrust-lawsuit-df9b552d127e1494db13e3cd625787a8 (AP)]
*Three people are killed and five others are injured in a [[shootout]] between two groups at a café in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]]. [https://metro.co.uk/2024/05/23/three-people-killed-a-gun-fight-istanbul-cafe-20900299/ (''Metro'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*The [[United Nations General Assembly]] votes 84–19, with 68 abstentions, to establish July 11 as an annual day of remembrance for the [[Srebrenica genocide]], despite receiving opposition from [[Serbia]] and [[Bosnian Serbs]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/23/un-approves-resolution-to-commemorate-1995-srebrenica-genocide (Al Jazeera)]
